sentences.text: Rajeev Kumar Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21
November, 2019

Author: Vishal Mishra
Bench: Vishal Mishra
 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 Mcrc-46606-2019
 (Rajeev Kumar Gupta Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh)
Gwalior, Dated :21/11/2019
 Shri V.K. Agarwal, learned counsel for the applicant.
 Shri Sanjay Bahirani, Public Prosecutor for the respondent-
State.
Case diary perused.
The applicant has filed this first application u/S.439, Cr.P.C. for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested by Police Station Special Task Force Bhopal, Unit Gwalior (M.P.), in connection with Crime No.12/2019 registered in relation to the offence punishable u/Ss.420, 272,
273, 120-B of IPC and u/S.51 and 59 of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

entities.text: Police Station Special Task Force Bhopal
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the matter.
He has not committed the offence in any manner.
The applicant is in custody since 9.9.2019.

It is alleged by the counsel for the applicant that in identical circumstances this Hon'ble Court vide its order dated 22.10.2019 passed in M.Cr.C. No.43734/2019 (Rajendra Prasad Gupta Vs. State of M.P.) has allowed the bail application of other co-accused, therefore, he claims parity with the other co-accused person and prays for grant of bail.

entities.text: Rajendra Prasad Gupta Vs. State of M.P.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH MCRC-46606-2019 (RAJEEV KUMAR GUPTA Vs THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH)

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH MCRC-46606-2019
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: RAJEEV KUMAR GUPTA Vs THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State has opposed the bail application and contended that the case of present applicant is not identical with the Rajendra Prasad Gupta and has contended that there is specific recovery from the possession of present applicant and articles are being found adulterated in the FSL report.
He fairly submits that there is no criminal antecedents against the present applicant.
He admits that investigation in the matter is over and charge-sheet has been filed on 27.9.2019 but he prays for dismissal of the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

sentences.text: Considering the submissions advanced by the counsel for the applicant and on perusal of the case diary it is seen that the investigation in the matter is complete and charge-sheet has been filed on 27.9.2019, therefore, no further custodial interrogation may be required in the matter, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to allow this application in the following terms.

It is hereby directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.1,00,000/-(Rupees One THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH MCRC-46606-2019 (RAJEEV KUMAR GUPTA Vs THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH) Lac Only) with two solvent sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court.

sentences.text: The applicant shall mark his attendance before the concerned police station in the first week of every month, till conclusion of investigation (pending if any) and if charge sheet is being filed, he will mark his presence as per the directions issued by the concerning trial Court.
A copy of this order be sent to the Court concerned for compliance.
Certified copy as per rules.

It is hereby directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.1,00,000/-(Rupees One THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH MCRC-46606-2019 (RAJEEV KUMAR GUPTA Vs THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH) Lac Only) with two solvent sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court.
